contract: `encoded` is the single `{key}` path segment in the reference form (spec rule 1); `decoded` is the key the server sees after its single percent-decode and equals `key` in every transmittable row (spec rules 3-4). Rows with `reject: true` are the keys spec rule 2 reserves (the empty key, `.`, `..`, `health`, `ttl`, `lock`): a conformant client raises before building the URL, so `encoded` and `decoded` are null. `encoded_alternates` lists the `encodeURIComponent` form (`! * ' ( )` raw) where it differs from `encoded`, and is absent otherwise; reject rows carry none. An SDK conforms when its encoding of `key` is in `[encoded] + encoded_alternates` (a missing `encoded_alternates` is `[]`).

vectors.note: Canonical 7-segment auto-mode key (test-vectors/cache-keys.json `single_integer`). Only `:` is encoded; identical bytes from all three reference encoders.
Embedded traversal: every `/` is `%2F`, so no `../` boundary exists for a URL parser to collapse. Server decodes once, then rejects (`/` outside charset; `..` substring).
Traversal aimed at the `/v1/cache/health` route token; inert once `/` is `%2F`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Query/fragment injection: `?` and `#` MUST be encoded or the client's URL parser truncates the key and emits a query string. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Space is `%20` in a path segment, never `+` (form-encoding, which the server does not decode). Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
A literal `%` is encoded exactly once; the server decodes once and sees `100%`, then rejects it (charset). `%2525` would decode to `100%25`, a different key.
Empty key: it encodes to an empty segment, so `/v1/cache/{key}` becomes `/v1/cache/` and `/v1/cache/{key}/ttl` becomes `/v1/cache//ttl`, neither of which addresses a stored entry.
Dot segment: the plain encoding `.` is removed by every URL parser, and `%2E` is collapsed by the server's WHATWG parse (`/v1/cache/%2E` → `/v1/cache/`). No wire form reaches the validator.
Dot segment: unencoded, `/v1/cache/..` collapses to `/v1/` and `/v1/cache/../ttl` to `/v1/ttl`; `%2E%2E` is collapsed the same way by the server's WHATWG parse. No wire form reaches the validator.
Route token: `/v1/cache/health` is the health endpoint, so a GET for this key would return the health payload as a cache hit.
Route token: a final `ttl` segment selects the TTL sub-resource, so `/v1/cache/ttl` is read as an empty key plus `/ttl`.
Route token: a final `lock` segment selects the lock sub-resource, so `/v1/cache/lock` is read as an empty key plus `/lock`.
Trailing dots but NOT an all-dot segment: not a dot segment under either parsing model, so the dots stay raw. Server rejects the decoded `..` substring.
Leading dots, not an all-dot segment: sent verbatim (all characters unreserved). Server rejects the decoded `..` substring.

`:` → `%3A`, decoded once server-side. The server then rejects it: a key starting `ns:` must be `ns:{namespace}:{rest}` with a non-empty `{rest}` (spec/cache-key-format.md § Server-Side Requirements, Namespace), and this one has no `{rest}`.

Encoder-variance row (spec rule 4): `quote(safe="")` and `urlencoding::encode` produce `encoded`; `encodeURIComponent` produces the alternate. Both decode to `key`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

Backslash traversal: a WHATWG URL parser reads a raw `\` as `/` in an `https` URL, so a raw `a\..\health` reaches `/v1/cache/health`. Sent as `%5C`, it is inert. Server rejects the decoded key (charset; `..` substring).

Tab between dots: a WHATWG URL parser strips every raw tab, LF and CR, so a tab left raw turns the key into `..`, a dot segment (`/v1/cache/..` collapses to `/v1/`). Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

CR and LF between dots: stripped like the tab above, so left raw they turn the key into `..`; a client that writes them raw into the request line also splits the request. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

Trailing space: a WHATWG URL parser strips spaces and C0 controls from both ends of the URL, so a raw one at the end of the key vanishes and `/v1/cache/.. ` collapses to `/v1/`. A request-path test catches this where it cannot see a raw mid-key space, which the parser encodes as `%20` itself. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

Trailing C0 control (VT, 0x0B): stripped from the end of the URL like the space above, so a raw one turns the request into `/v1/cache/health`, the health endpoint. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Control characters at the ends of their ranges: NUL (0x00), US (0x1F, the last C0 control) and DEL (0x7F) are each sent as `%HH`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

An existing percent-escape is data: its `%` is `%25`, like any other. An encoder that keeps a valid escape raw, as never-double-encode encoders do, sends `%2e%2e`, which the server's WHATWG parse reads as a dot segment: `/v1/cache/%2e%2e/ttl` becomes `/v1/ttl`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset: `%`).
Non-ASCII, two UTF-8 bytes: U+00E9 is `%C3%A9`, never its Latin-1 byte `%E9` (which JavaScript's `escape()` writes). Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

Non-ASCII, four UTF-8 bytes: U+1F600 is `%F0%9F%98%80`, never its two UTF-16 surrogates encoded one by one (`%ED%A0%BD%ED%B8%80`, or `escape()`'s `%uD83D%uDE00`). Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Non-ASCII, three UTF-8 bytes: U+2025 TWO DOT LEADER. An encoder that NFKC-normalises the key first turns it into `..`, a dot segment. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Unreserved `-` and `~` stay raw, never `%2D` or `%7E` (Python's `quote` escaped `~` before 3.7). Server rejects the decoded key (charset: `~`).
Uppercase letters are unreserved and stay raw. The server accepts this key (the `default` namespace), so these are the wire bytes rule 4 says every SDK sends for it.

As the `%2e%2e` row: an encoder that keeps `%3A` raw makes the server decode it to `:`, so the request reads and writes the entry of `User:Key`, the storable key in the row above. Server rejects the decoded key (charset: `%`).

`+ & ; , @ $` are legal raw in a path segment, so an encoder with a path-segment safe set (`encodeURI`, or RFC 3986's `pchar`) leaves them raw, and a WHATWG parser leaves `[ ]` raw too. Rule 1 encodes all eight, and `+` is `%2B`, never a space. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).

Printable ASCII that RFC 3986 allows in no URL component: `" < > ^ { | }` and the backtick (the space and backslash rows hold the other two). Rule 1 encodes each. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
